graph.agentCount: dynamic; use as many agents as safe and useful, not a fixed role count
graph.edgeComputationLaw: a conflict graph must compute an edge for EVERY edgeWhen condition, not only shared writable files. Condition 3 (one lane consumes anatomy concurrently changed by another) is computed from real imports resolving into another lane scope; conditions 2 and 4 are computed from declared shared authority and generated/i18n domain ownership. A condition that is asserted rather than computed is not satisfied.
graph.readSetRequired: every writing node must declare an exact readSet. Without it condition 3 cannot be computed and the graph silently degrades to write/write only, which is what made an incomplete plan read as conflict-free.

barrelOwnership.why: reservedPaths protects SHARED BARRELS, and family-writer.mayNotEdit names `barrels` for the same reason. But this package's structure law makes every authored production unit a `folder/index.ts`, so the literal glob `packages/core/src/**/index.ts` also matches each family's own implementation entrypoint. Classifying by FILENAME would neutralise a binding rule wholesale; classifying by POSITION adjudicates it. This block is the canonical adjudication — a checker must read the rule from here rather than hardcode one.
barrelOwnership.familyRootAuthority: the writeSet roots declared by the family-writer lanes of the round's ownership proposal. If those roots are not supplied, the rule cannot classify and the fail-closed disposition applies.

classes.shared-barrel: an index file whose directory either (i) lies OUTSIDE every declared family root, or (ii) is a STRICT ANCESTOR of any declared family root. Either way it sits above peer owners and aggregates them. Condition (ii) is what stops a lane from laundering a category barrel into its own source merely by declaring the category as its root.
classes.implementation-entrypoint: an index file whose directory is AT or INSIDE a declared family root AND is not a strict ancestor of any declared family root. It is that family's own authored source.
classes.unclassified: the hit directory lies inside family roots of MORE THAN ONE lane, or familyRoots is empty or unavailable, or any case the predicate does not decide. Owned by nobody; blocking.

barrelOwnership.implementationEntrypointOwner: the family-writer whose declared family root contains it
barrelOwnership.note: the reserved pattern ends in `.ts` and therefore does not match `.tsx`. That asymmetry is not relied upon by this rule: classification is positional and applies to whatever the reserved pattern matched.

familyRootDerivation.derive: every family-writer lane writeSet entry of the round proposal with the trailing /** removed, plus every families[].sourceOwner in the proposal that lies STRICTLY inside one of that same lane's writeSet roots (nested family markers, attributed to that lane)
familyRootDerivation.law: sourceOwner is a resolution pointer, never a write boundary; it may enter familyRoots only through the strictly-inside filter above
familyRootDerivation.containment: per path segment: A is inside B iff A equals B or A starts with B plus a slash; strict containment excludes equality

barrelOwnership.extensionLaw: a shared barrel is a pure re-export module and is therefore index.ts; index.tsx is an authored component entrypoint and is never a shared barrel. The .ts spelling of appliesToReservedPattern is deliberate, not an accident of extension — structures/shell/index.tsx being unreserved is CORRECT because it is the AppShell component.
failClosed: a hit on any reserved pattern other than appliesToReservedPattern is outside this adjudication and blocks unconditionally
an absent barrelOwnership rule blocks every hit of the adjudicated pattern
a classification never excuses an ownership collision; collisions are computed independently and stay blocking
barrelOwnership.bindsMayNotEditCategoryWhy: laneTypes[family-writer].mayNotEdit lists "barrels", but it is enforced by a substring test for a directory named barrels/ which exists nowhere in this tree — the category has been vacuous since inception. Binding it to the classifier makes the word enforceable without touching laneTypes.
barrelOwnership.consumerParityLaw: both consumers MUST route through the single exported classifier. A second, checker-local semantics is void: one code path neutralising the contract the other enforces is the defect this block exists to prevent.
barrelOwnership.localOwnershipLaw: classification answers what KIND of file a reserved hit is; it never grants a lane the right to write it. Both consumers call the one shared classifier. Inside the proposal analyzer, owning-lane agreement is a STRUCTURAL invariant: a family-writer expansion derives from its own writeSet, every writeSet entry is a derived family root, so a permitted verdict cannot name a foreign lane, and a file inside two lanes roots fails closed as unclassified. A lane PACKET has no such guarantee — it is a runtime claim constructed outside the proposal — so admission must additionally resolve packet.lane to exactly one proposal lane and require owningLane equality on every adjudicated hit. Same classifier, same law, two subjects. A consumer may consume MORE of the shared verdict than the other surfaces; it may never contradict it. Discarding owningLane was the parity defect this law closes. The analyzer ASSERTS its invariant executably rather than assuming it: a permitted entry whose owningLane differs from the lane it was found under is reclassified blocking.
barrelOwnership.admissionRequiresProposal: a packet of ANY writing lane class (family-writer, architecture-integrator, quality-integrator) cannot be admitted without the authorized ownership proposal supplied explicitly by the caller. It is never inferred from the evidence root or from the packet itself. Absent proposal is an evaluation blocker, not a usage error, so the refusal is machine-readable. Reviewers are exempt because they may own no files at all, which is enforced separately.
barrelOwnership.laneBindingScope: lane resolution and effective-write-set containment bind every writing lane class, not only family-writer. Scoping them to family-writer would leave an integrator packet free to claim a family entrypoint with no ownership check, since the reserved-path loop is itself family-writer scoped.
barrelOwnership.newFileAdmissibilityLaw: workOrderAdmission.requiredBeforeWrite means admission runs BEFORE the lane writes, so a file the lane is about to create does not exist. An existing owned file is judged against effectiveFiles, the exported authority the closure names. A NOT-YET-EXISTING owned file is judged against the same lane writeSet minus writeSetExcludes over patterns (laneScopeContains), which is no weaker — the path must still fall inside the lane declared authority — and without it the gate would be unsatisfiable for exactly the work it authorizes, deadlocking the quality-integrator whose charter is writing new tests. The two are required to agree on every file that exists, and that agreement is drilled over the whole R0 proposal rather than argued.

r1AggressiveExecution.writerTopology: Multiple Opus writers on exact disjoint worktrees; multiple Sonnet scouts prepare current and next slices; one architecture integrator and one quality integrator; Fable and Codex audit the integrated candidate at their governed cadence.
r1AggressiveExecution.sourceBudget: At least 80 percent product source and visible quality; at most 20 percent tooling, audit and evidence. No new instrument unless an existing instrument cannot measure a named blocker.
r1AggressiveExecution.toolingMoratorium: No new Modern Rescue script, gate, census, drill or evidence format during R1 unless the packet names a blocking claim that no existing command can measure and both Fable and Codex confirm the gap. Prefer deleting, merging or extending an existing capability.
r1AggressiveExecution.manifestEntryPoint: packages/core/scripts/generate/tokens/manifest/generation/index.mjs must become the single real write/check/certify entrypoint. Current limitation is explicit: it syncs schema and authored cells but does not derive actual compiler/CSS dependencies or hash all productive sources. Extend this file, not the script count, to emit declared/observed/gap edges and bind certification to source plus computed evidence. Run it once per integrated batch; never hand-edit generated rollups.
r1AggressiveExecution.toolingConsolidation: A bounded Sonnet mechanical lane audits and consolidates all of packages/core/scripts without blocking product writers. The target is descriptive domain/subdomain/capability/index.mjs: capabilities with related behavior share a named subdomain, single-child or generic wrappers are forbidden, and the path explains the command without knowing an agent, work order, round or historical execution. Root exceptions are forbidden. Public package/CI callers receive tested path updates or a temporary compatibility shim; dead entrypoints, duplicate scanners and recursive suites are removed. First candidates are the recursive sub-suite runner in program-check.test, non-consumable cascade-materialize/backlog outputs, and duplicate CSS census after fanout-facts absorbs the unique cascade-extract fact. cascade-probe remains only if a release caller is named. Test artifacts follow the same semantic rule but signed evidence moves only with complete reference and digest reanchoring. No replacement platform or new structural gate: evolve scripts-tree-gate to enforce the target hierarchy as each migration batch lands.
r1AggressiveExecution.autonomy: Do not wait for the owner on reversible in-scope corrections. Kimi resolves source-grounded Fable/Codex disagreement and continues. Stop only for product/commercial scope, incompatible public API, destructive or external actions, release, publish or push.
